findings.text: Packet drop helper releases the supplied packet with the given drop reason and returns a combined verdict that carries a caller error in the high half together with a stolen indication. The error is constrained at build time to fit in sixteen bits.

Address helpers operate on a sixteen byte protocol independent address union. One predicate reports equality of two addresses. One writer stores the conjunction of an address and a mask into a result. The fragments show two build dependent internal strategies with identical external meaning.

Hook invocation context carries a hook identifier, a protocol family, ingress and egress device references, an associated socket, a network namespace reference, and a completion callback used when filtering accepts. An initializer fills all of those members from caller arguments.

Registration descriptor links into a list, carries deferred free state, a filter callback, an optional bound device, private data, family, category tag, hook number and priority. Runtime dispatch uses a compact entry of callback plus private. The active table stores a sixteen bit count followed by a variable length entry array, with a trailer holding original descriptors and deferred free state located immediately past the array.
Filter category tag defines five successive values meaning undefined, tables based filtering, packet filter program, fast track tables variant, and address translation.

Primary filter entry selects a per network namespace hook table by family for version four, version six, address resolution and bridge families, under read side protection, initializes a stack context from caller arguments, and delegates to a slow iterator when a table is present. Absent tables or disabled builds accept immediately. Unknown families and out of range address resolution indexes take a one time warning path.

Convenience wrappers encode the accept continuation contract. A verdict meaning accept proceeds to the caller completion callback, other verdicts propagate unchanged. One conditional form skips filtering when its predicate is false. One list form feeds a queued packet list through the table without returning a verdict. Disabled builds reduce to direct completion or to no operation for the list form.

Hook table lookup and slow iteration execute inside a read side critical section that starts before family selection and ends after iteration. Address translation session decoding likewise dereferences its global hook pointer only while holding the same protection.

Several operation tables expose callback pointers for extension. Socket option table carries family, get and set ranges with handlers and owner. Translation table carries setup parsing, session decoding and cleanup by source. Tracking table carries update, destroy, tuple extraction, attach, closing mark, confirm and identifier. Netlink tracking table carries size, build, parse, expect attach and sequence adjust. Defragmentation table carries owner with enable and disable.

Translation session decoding dispatches through a globally installed hook only when enabled and when a handler is present, otherwise it does nothing. This header provides inert tracking attach, closing mark and tuple lookup that respectively do nothing and report failure. Real behavior is delegated to the installed tracking hook table.

Tracking statistics record unsigned counters for lookup outcomes, insertion, clash resolution, drops, errors, expectation lifecycle, restarts and overlong chains. A tracking reference object holds a single reference count. A zone descriptor holds a sixteen bit identifier plus flag and direction bytes.

Info field uses low three bits with value seven as mask and inverted mask for pointer extraction. Default zone identifier is zero, direction bits cover original and reply with combined default, and mark flag uses value one. Address resolution family defines three hooks, and the maximum hook count aliases the internet family hook count.
Tracking reference management ignores null input. Get increments the count. Put decrements and destroys the object only when the count reaches zero.

Version four route info carries destination, source, service type and mark. Version six variant carries destination, source and mark with larger addresses. An extension header predicate recognizes hop options, routing, fragment, encapsulating security, authentication, no next header and destination options.

Version four checksum helper in this fragment always reports zero and its route helper always reports operation not supported. Version six helpers delegate to real implementations when version six is enabled and otherwise report fixed fallbacks: address check accepts, route and reroute report unreachable, fragment accepts, cookie sequence and check report zero.

Netlink control block overlay carries credentials, port identifier, destination group, flags, socket, and optional namespace identifier state. Kernel configuration carries group count, flags, input, bind, unbind and release handlers. Extended acknowledgement carries message pointer, offending attribute, policy, missing nesting info, cookie with length, and formatted message buffer. Dump callback carries packet, header, dump and done handlers, data, module, extended acknowledgement, family, answer flags, allocation hint, sequence state, flags, strict flag, and a fixed size context area that also overlays legacy long arguments. Notify descriptor carries network namespace, port and protocol.

Non root receive and send configuration use the lowest two bits. Destination set flag uses bit three. Cookie capacity is eight bytes and formatted message capacity is eighty bytes. Callback context size is forty eight bytes. Default message size is good size minus header length, where good size follows page size on one build and a fixed eight kilobyte base on the other.

Header accessor interprets packet data as a netlink header. Kernel socket creation forwards to an internal creator with the current module. Clone helper duplicates a packet and preserves the destructor when the head resides in virtual allocation. Cookie setter copies an eight byte value when acknowledgement storage is present. Filter type describes a socket packet data predicate. Extended acknowledgement helpers record messages, offending attributes with policy, missing attributes and required attribute checks, tolerating absent storage and warning when formatted output truncates.

Hooks are ordered by ascending priority. Table count bounds the entry array and the original descriptor array begins exactly past the last entry. Tracking pointer tagging reserves low bits for info. Callback private context must fit within the fixed context area, enforced by a build time assertion.

Out of range hook selection and unexpected families take warning paths rather than silent dispatch. Formatted extended acknowledgement helpers emit a rate limited warning when output is truncated. Reference release destroys the tracked object only when the last reference drops. Callers must handle null tracking pointers.
Headers use include guards that define a per header macro on first inclusion to prevent repeated processing.
External read side lock relied upon around hook lookup.
External read side unlock relied upon after hook iteration.
External protected pointer read relied upon for hook tables and NAT hook.
External static branch query relied upon for hook fast path bypass.
Alternate build of static branch query relied upon for hook fast path bypass.
External virtual address test relied upon during netlink clone.
External decrement and test relied upon for tracking release.
External increment relied upon for tracking get.
